extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutional grant administrators preparing NIH and AHRQ grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on NIH/AHRQ policy changes that allow resubmitted (A1) proposals to be submitted as new (A0) applications, including timing, overlap rules, required forms, and content expectations. Useful for applicants deciding whether to submit a new application or a resubmission and for administrative staff advising investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: No assessment of similarity for A0 accepted after A1
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH and AHRQ will not assess the similarity of the science in the new (A0) application to any previously reviewed submission when accepting an application for review. (NOT-OD-14-074)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application submitted as a new A0 will not be judged at the time of acceptance by how similar its science is to prior reviewed submissions; acceptance for review does not trigger similarity comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: No introduction responding to previous critiques in A0
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application need not demonstrate substantial changes in scientific direction compared to previously reviewed submissions, and must not contain an introduction to respond to the critiques from the previous review. (NOT-OD-14-074)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting as a new A0 instead of an A1/resubmission, do not include an 'Introduction' whose purpose is to address prior reviewers' critiques; treat the application as a fresh submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on duplicate or highly overlapping applications under simultaneous review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s policy for accepting overlapping applications remains in effect (NOT-OD-09-100) and NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically NIH will not accept: (a) a new (A0) application submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of an overlapping resubmission (A1); (b) a resubmission (A1) submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application; (c) an application that has substantial overlap with another application pending appeal of initial peer review (NOT-OD-11-101). Ensure timing to avoid simultaneous overlapping submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to submit as new A0 after prior review (timing rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that was reviewed before April 16th, 2014, as well as any application submitted in the future, could be submitted as a new (A0) application for any subsequent, appropriate due date, if the previous summary statement has been released. (NOT-OD-14-082)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit a previously reviewed application as a new A0 provided the summary statement from the prior review has been issued; check release of summary statement before filing as A0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to major application types and activity codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated policy applies to major types of applications and activity codes - including applications for research grants, the NIH SBIR and STTR programs, Career Development Awards, Individual Fellowships, Institutional Training Grants, Resource Grants, Program Projects, and Center Grants. (NOT-OD-14-082)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is broad across many NIH/AHRQ mechanisms; verify applicability to your specific activity code but generally includes the listed categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on number of submission cycles; applicants encouraged to update content
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of submission cycles is not limited, but NIH encourages applicants to update their applications to reflect the status of the field over the interim period and to incorporate new preliminary data, literature citations, letters of reference, etc. as time passes. (NOT-OD-14-082)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although you may submit repeatedly, you should improve and update the application between submissions (new data, citations, letters) rather than re-submit unchanged material.

rubrics_metrics.name: New A0 allowed after unsuccessful A0 without intervening A1
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated policy does not preclude submission of a new (A0) application following an unsuccessful new (A0) application, without an intervening resubmission (A1) application. (NOT-OD-14-082)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an A0 was not successful, you may re-submit as another new A0 without first filing an A1; treat it as a fresh submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No overall limit on times an application can be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of times an application can be submitted. (FAQ Item A.7)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may attempt multiple cycles; plan strategy (new vs resubmission) each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case decision: submit new application vs resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant should decide on a case by case basis whether it is better to submit a new application or to address the reviewer’s statement in a resubmission of the previous application. (FAQ Item B.4)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the nature of critiques, new data, and strategic factors when choosing between A0 and A1 paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing renewal (Type 2) resubmission rule: submit as new Type 1 A0 after unsuccessful resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: After a resubmission of a competing renewal (Type 2) application that is not funded the next submission should be submitted as a new application (Type 1 A0) on the new application due date, and it will lose any association with the previously funded grant. (FAQ Item B.7)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a new Type 1, the application is due on the new application due date (not renewal due date) and must not contain a Progress Report or an introduction responding to previous critiques; it will not be linked to the prior grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submission to different FOA/RFA considered a new application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not successful through the RFA and is late submitted to a different RFA or to a program announcement (such as the 'parent' announcement), then it is considered a new application. If your application was submitted previously to a PA and you want to now submit it to an RFA, it is considered a new application. (FAQ Item B.11)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the funding opportunity announcement (e.g., PA to RFA) or late transfer to another FOA converts the submission status to 'new'—follow new application rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form/package required by the FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are applying to a new funding opportunity announcement (FOA), you must use the form (proposal package) associated with that FOA. When submitting to the same FOA as the previous application, check the funding opportunity to make sure that no form updates have happened since the previous submission. If a more recent version is available, the information will need to be transferred to the new proposal package. (FAQ Item C.3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always verify and use the correct electronic forms for the target FOA; if forms changed, migrate your content into the updated package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reference prior submissions in cover letter for new A0
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new application is being submitted in the same topic area of science as an unfunded resubmission application, no reference to the previous submissions should be made in the cover letter of the new application. The application will be given a new number and will not be compared to the previous submissions. (FAQ Item C.5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the new A0 as independent; avoid mentioning past submission history in cover letter to prevent linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title may remain unchanged when submitting as new
rubrics_metrics.description: The title an application being submitted again as new does not need to be changed unless the applicant wishes to change the title. (FAQ Item C.9)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the title is optional when converting a previously submitted application into a new A0; not required by policy.
